new_statements.translation: As for tonology, my documents show no difference from M[ongo] (Grammaire du lomongo I, p. 132), except na 'who', ndélé 'tile', nkélé 'anger', versus Mongo ná, ndɛlɛ, nkɛlɛ. These isolated cases remain unexplained.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (200 pp., whole Annales Aequatoria 5, scanned text layer; Hulstaert 1984 'La langue des Mpama' = PDF pp. 5-32). I rendered printed p. 7 (PDF p. 7) at 150 dpi and read the image: the paragraph is there exactly where the locator says (Premiere partie: Phonologie, I. Les voyelles, last paragraph before 'II. CONSONNES'): 'Pour la tonologie mes documents ne présentent pas de différence avec M (Gr.I,p.132), hormis na qui, ndɛ́lɛ́ tuile, nkɛ́lɛ́ colère, contre M ná, ndɛlɛ, nkɛlɛ. Ces cas isolés demeurent inexpliqués.' Only difference from the reported quote: the Mpama forms are typed with epsilon-plus-acute glyphs (ndɛ́lɛ́, nkɛ́lɛ́), which the first reader rendered as ndélé/nkélé; wo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mpama is described as a tone language whose (lexical and grammatical) tone system is the same as Lomongo's; tones are marked throughout the sketch and tonal behaviour of prefixes and verb endings is discussed in the morphology. The source says nothing at all about word stress/accent — no claim of its presence, position, or absence.
new_statements.exceptions: Only three lexical items whose tones differ from Mongo (na, ndélé, nkélé); nothing concerning stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Tonal remarks concern words and inflected verb forms from 120 elicited sentences (one speaker, Bonginda village near Lukolela); no phrase-level prosody or accent discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Hulstaert 1984 describes the speech of one speaker (J. Nkéké) from Bonginda village, Mpámá tribe ('Bakutu' to neighbours), hinterland of the left bank of the Congo at Lukolela (c. 17°E, 1°S) — this is Glottolog's Mpama [mpam1239] (no ISO code; Ethnologue folds it under Mongo-Nkundu lol). Hulstaert himself notes he cannot say how far the described variety extends or what dialect differences exist within Mpama.

sources.note: Nothing. 'Premiere partie: Phonologie' (pp. 6-8) = vowels (with one paragraph on 'tonologie', p. 7: tone system does not differ from Mongo, Hulstaert Grammaire du lomongo I p. 132, apart from three isolated lexical items), consonants, elisions; the morphology (pp. 8-32) marks and discusses tones of prefixes/TAM endings throughout. No mention of accent/stress anywhere in pp. 5-32 (scanned text a full-text search for stress/accent accen/intens; pages 6-8 read from images). Based on 120 translated survey sentences from one speaker of Bonginda village.
